stories.title: Nvidia sinks after report implicates CEO Jensen Huang in 2nd affair
stories.summary: Shares in Nvidia sank Wednesday night after the New York Times reported CEO Jensen Huang had a second affair with a senior executive who reports to him. Why it matters: The report adds to mounting scrutiny of Huang, already under investigation over an affair with a purported Chinese spy. The potential impact goes beyond one man and one business, though. Huang is arguably the world's most powerful...

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Nvidia board meeting to decide CEO Jensen Huang’s fate stretches into evening
sources.text: Nvidia's board is meeting to decide whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang , CNBC confirmed late Wednesday, following reports of two extramarital affairs — one with an employee and another with an alleged Chinese spy. Shares of Nvidia fell more than 9% in post-market trading after The Wall Street Journal first reported that the board was preparing to force out Huang. That news landed minutes after The New York Times reported that Huang had a romantic relationship with Nvidia's vice president of health care. The alleged relationship, according to the Times story, was with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at Nvidia. Powell's bio on the Nvidia website says she's "responsible for the company's worldwide healthcare business, including hardware and software platforms for accelerated computing, AI, and visualization that power the ecosystem of medical imaging, life sciences, drug discovery, and healthcare analytics." Huang and Powell were reportedly captured on camera being affectionate with one another at a hotel in San Jose, California in March, according to the Times. Nvidia and Powell didn't respond to CNBC's request for comment. Heller, the crisis PR firm Huang reportedly hired as early as last year, did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment. The report comes days after Huang admitted to an affair with a woman who is believed by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy. The CEO was romantically involved with Alice Huang, according to The Financial Times , who U.S. intelligence officials believe is a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, The New York Times reported. Nvidia's board of directors has opened an independent investigation and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to look into the spying allegations. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Huang wrote in the message to Nvidia staff on Sunday. "I am deeply sorry." Most of Huang's Nvidia shares are co-owned with his wife, Lori Huang, and are held in trusts. About 800 million shares are held by those trusts. Huang holds about 70 million shares on his own and has limited economic control over the company. Rumors of an affair between Huang and Powell have circulated for years, in part because Powell lacks a background in health or science, according to a former employee who asked not to be named because of the sensitivity of the matter. Healthcare is a smaller business at Nvidia. The company makes chips for medical devices and MRI machines, but they are a minor in comparison to the revenue generated from its advanced AI systems and graphics processing units, or GPUs. In recent appearances, including at the company's annual GTC conference, Powell has spoken about how Nvidia's AI technology can help accelerate drug discovery, assist providers and improve clinical efficiency. Powell has been leading the group since 2017. Nvidia's stock was down 7% this week prior to the after-hours drop on Wednesday and is on pace for its sixth straight weekly slide, reflecting broad concern on the sustainability of the artificial intelligence buildout. The AI infrastructure trade was hit particularly hard last week after the midterm elections, as Democrats won sweeping majorities in both houses of Congress, and dozens of ballot measures past that could make building data centers more difficult. Huang has become synonymous with the AI industry, and he is often referred to by his first name ,"Jensen," by customers and rivals. Nvidia has been one of the primary beneficiaries of the AI boom since its chips are used to train models and run large AI workloads. —CNBC's Lora Kolodny and Kif Leswing contributed to this report WATCH: Jensen Huang said to have had relationship with Nvidia executive who reports to him: New York Times

sources.title: Nvidia board reportedly deciding whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang as stock price plunges
sources.text: Meeting comes after CEO admitted to having a relationship with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy Nvidia’s board of directors met on Wednesday to decide whether to oust Jensen Huang as CEO of the world’s most valuable chip company, according to multiple reports, after a tumultuous week in which the executive and co-founder of the company admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. The meeting marks ⁠a sharp shift from Sunday, when Nvidia’s board ​expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team. However, Huang’s position became more tenuous late on Wednesday after it was reported by the New York Times that Huang had a separate extramarital affair with a company employee named Kimberly Powell. She was Nvidia’s president of healthcare and was reportedly captured on video being affectionate with Huang at a hotel during a company conference in March. The company’s stock slid more than 8% in after-hours trading after the Wall Street Journal reported that ⁠the company was preparing to fire Huang. If those losses hold, Nvidia will have lost about $685bn (£516bn) in market value since the board announced its investigation into his relationship with a businesswoman, Alice Huang, who is accused of being a Chinese spy. “The market is starting to price Nvidia without its founder as the likely outcome, not ‌a tail risk,” said Armina Rosenberg, a portfolio manager and the co-founder ‌of Minotaur Capital, which holds Nvidia shares. Dan Ives, a US tech analyst, said the company “likely now has to move on without Jensen at the helm”. Under Nvidia’s bylaws, Huang can be removed “with or without cause” by a majority vote of directors. Nvidia has 11 directors and considers all but Huang independent. The board’s independent directors this week appointed the leading law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a “thorough and independent” investigation into the relationship. The firm directed Huang to continue to helm Nvidia as the investigation was ongoing. Huang is seen as the ambitious and visionary leader of Nvidia, a company he co-founded in 1993. His exit would leave a leadership vacuum at a time when the AI arms race between the US and China is at an apex. He has no obvious successor, and personally owns more than 870m shares, or about 3.6% of the company, making him the world’s 13th richest person according to Bloomberg. Unlike many of his contemporaries at other big tech companies, Huang has dozens of direct reports, an unusual management structure that emphasises his control over the company. The entire artificial intelligence ecosphere relies on the company, which engineers advanced chips used to train AI models and power companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. It is also one of the most valuable companies on earth, with a market cap of more than $4tn. Huang himself is one of the world’s richest people, with an estimated net worth of $148bn. While Huang admitted to having an affair – without naming Alice Huang directly – he denied any knowledge that the woman allegedly worked for the Chinese government, according to Trump. The Nvidia CEO and the Chinese businesswoman, an Nvidia customer, were seen together around the world, dining in restaurants and attending meetings, over the past few years. Alice Huang is an executive at the Singapore-based datacentre firm Megaspeed, which uses Nvidia chips. On Thursday a Taiwanese government minister said Alice Huang had visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, as he responded to questions about a New York Times report that claimed the US had advised Taiwan as early as 2024 to monitor her movements. Chiu Chui-cheng, Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council minister, said there were “no special flags” about her at the time, Chiu said, adding that “if we had any of the kind of critical intelligence … we would have definitely flagged her for heightened review.” Jensen Huang, who has been married to his wife, Lori, since 1985, admitted in an email to employees on Sunday that he had an affair and that he would cooperate with an internal investigation. Nvidia’s board of directors put out a statement the same day that the company was launching an investigation regarding reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Donald Trump has backed Huang , saying he had done “an incredible job” and is “an honorable guy”. Leading tech industry players, including Elon Musk, have also thrown their support behind Huang. Musk was asked on X early on Thursday if he would hire a jobless Huang. He replied: “That would be an honour”. Democratic senators Elizabeth Warren ⁠and Chris Coons have asked the Trump administration to preserve all documents tied to Nvidia’s chip ⁠exports to China, it was revealed late on Wednesday. “This ‌incident raises significant ‌concerns about the federal government’s ability to effectively enforce our export ‌controls and protect our national security,” the senators said in the letter sent to commerce secretary Howard Lutnick, secretary of state Marco Rubio and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller. Nvidia did not immediately return a request for comment.

sources.title: NVIDIA shareholders are suing the company and CEO Jensen Huang
sources.text: The company’s shares have plummeted in response to the exec’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The unfolding drama around NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman now accused of being a spy for the Chinese government may be getting its first courtroom chapter. A shareholder in the computing giant has sued accusing NVIDIA and Huang of misleading investors about the nature of the CEO's relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Taiwanese company Megaspeed who is now suspected of being an espionage asset for China. Huang is a common surname; The pair are not related. Mark Kistenmacher filed the complaint and is seeking class action status for anyone who purchased NVIDIA shares between October 9 and November 8. The first date is when The New York Times published a story on NVIDIA and Megaspeed detailing a connection between the pair, which was rebuffed by NVIDIA as a routine business relationship; the second date is when the NVIDIA founder admitted to an affair and the company publicly disclosed that it was launching its own investigation into whether its top exec had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. In the interim, The New York Times published an in-depth feature on October 29 claiming that the NVIDIA CEO had become the subject of a suspected Chinese intelligence action. The piece cites NVIDIA representative John Rizzo, who said, "Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year." This statement, the lawsuit alleges, was not true. The company's shares have dropped in the fallout of the allegations, with NVIDIA on track to lose more than $470 billion in market value over the past two days. "As a result of Defendants' wrongful acts and omissions, and the precipitous decline in the market value of the Company's securities, Plaintiff and other Class members have suffered significant losses and damages," the complaint states.

Nvidia has become one of the most valuable companies in the world as it designs the chips that power the AI boom, but in the midst of Huang’s ongoing scandal , Nvidia stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday. The stock is down about 11% in the past five days. Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . sources.title: Nvidia’s board reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after reports of a second affair
sources.text: Nvidia Corp.’s board of directors is reportedly preparing to oust its founder and Chief Executive Jensen Huang after reports emerged that he had a second extramarital relationship with an executive at the company, just days after he admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Earlier today, the New York Times said Huang (pictured) was suspected by five people at the company of having an affair with Nvidia Healthcare Vice President Kimberly Powell. Hours later, the Wall Street Journal said Nvidia’s board is preparing to meet on Thursday to discuss Huang’s future at the company, and that all options are on the table, including his possible dismissal. The Times said Huang and Powell were reportedly captured on camera together being affectionate with one another at a hotel in San Jose, California, in March. The latest reports come just days after Huang admitted in an email to company employees that he had an extramarital affair with a Chinese woman called Alice Huang, who was formerly the CEO of the Singaporean data center supplier Megaspeed. Alice Huang, of no relation to Nvidia’s CEO, is suspected of working for China’s Ministry of State Security, but it’s not clear if she has passed on any of the company’s secrets. In response to that report, Nvidia’s board hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead an investigation into the affair and try to determine what secrets, if any, were leaked. Huang reportedly first became involved with the Chinese woman last year, but rumors of an affair between him and Powell have circulated for years. One reason for that is that Powell does not have any background in health or science, despite her high-level role at Nvidia’s Healthcare business. On Nvidia’s website, Powell’s bio explains that she’s responsible for the company’s healthcare business, “including hardware and software platforms for accelerated computing, AI and visualization that power the ecosystem of medical imaging, life sciences, drug discovery and healthcare analytics.” The Healthcare business is much smaller than Nvidia’s main data center unit, which accounts for the lion’s share of its multibillion-dollar revenue. It makes chips for medical devices such as MRI machines. The company does not break out sales figures for the unit, instead reporting its revenue within the broader data center business. Powell appeared at Nvidia’s annual GTC conference in San Jose in March, where she delivered a keynote talking about how the company’s AI technology can help to accelerate drug discovery and enhance clinical efficiency. She has been running the business since 2017. If Nvidia were to oust Huang, the company that sits at the heart of the artificial intelligence revolution would face an uncertain future. Nvidia is the second most valuable company in the world, controlling around 90% of the global market for computer chips used in AI, becoming a major driving force behind the global economy. Its brand has become synonymous with Huang, who is involved in all aspects of its business and has appointed family members to key roles in its executive team. Huang is also Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, holding a 3.56% stake in the company. Should he be ousted, there is no clear successor. Nvidia’s rise amid the AI boom has made Huang one of the wealthiest and most influential people in the world. He has become a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, who was previously told about Huang’s relationship with the suspected Chinese spy but decided to take no action. Trump has come out in defense of Huang , saying that he’s an “honorable man” and that he did not know of the woman’s connections to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia’s stock fell more than 9% in late trading on Wednesday and is likely to extend its downward trend for a sixth straight week. sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Elon Musk says it would be an 'honor' to hire Nvidia's Jensen Huang
sources.text: SpaceX founder and Tesla CEO Elon Musk said it would be "an honor" to hire embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , after reports emerged that Nvidia's board could be preparing to oust Huang from the company. Late Wednesday stateside, financial blog Zerohedge wrote on X, "Elon please hire Jensen," to which Musk replied , "That would be an honor." The post comes as the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to discuss Huang's future at the company. The report also followed a New York Times story that Huang had an extramarital relationship with another Nvidia executive. The developments sent Nvidia shares down more than 8% in after-hours trading. Huang and Nvidia have dominated headlines since the weekend after the Nvidia CEO acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a business executive whom U.S. intelligence identified as having been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security. Alice Huang, also known by her Chinese name Huang Le, was recruited to gather information on Jensen, according to people briefed on the intelligence cited by The New York Times. The Nvidia chief sought to project a "business as usual" atmosphere on his first day back at the office after the revelations, but he is now facing calls to resign from several lawmakers. Sen. Kevin Cramer , R-N.D., a member of the Senate Banking Committee, reiterated Wednesday his call for Huang to resign, joining Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., a member of the House Oversight Committee and Rep. Don Bacon , R-Neb., who is retiring from Congress. "As a matter of his own conscience, he should resign," Cramer told CNBC.

sources.title: Elon Musk, dueño de Tesla, abre la puerta a contratar a Jensen Huang si lo despiden como CEO de NVIDIA: "Sería un honor"
sources.text: Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google. Elon Musk ha expresado su interés en contratar a Jensen Huang si abandona el puesto de CEO de NVIDIA tras las polémicas relacionadas con una supuesta infidelidad con una espía china y con Kimberly Powell. Elon Musk ha dejado abierta la puerta a contratar a Jensen Huang si NVIDIA decide apartarlo de la dirección ejecutiva. El CEO de SpaceX respondió a un mensaje de ZeroHedge en X que le pedía fichar al cofundador del fabricante de chips. Cabe señalar que esta reacción llega después de que The Wall Street Journal informara de que la junta directiva se prepara para estudiar su destitución . Musk, sin embargo, no ha anunciado una oferta ni hay nada confirmado de conversaciones con Huang . La crisis se ha intensificado por informaciones sobre dos supuestas infidelidades del directivo y sus posibles implicaciones para la compañía. El consejo anunció abrir una investigación después de las noticias que apuntaban a que Huang podría haber sido objetivo de espionaje . La segunda relación, con una directiva de NVIDIA, se conoció días después. La primera controversia gira en torno a Alice Huang, antigua directiva de Megaspeed International , una empresa de Singapur vinculada comercialmente a NVIDIA. Varias fuentes informaron de que los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses sospechaban que podía trabajar para China. Y también se investigan posibles desvíos de chips de la compañía hacia empresas chinas, en un contexto de restricciones de Estados Unidos a la exportación de procesadores avanzados. Jensen Huang reconoció ante sus empleados que había sido infiel a su esposa y pidió disculpas, aunque no identificó a la mujer en su mensaje. Cabe mencionar que la segunda información apunta a Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de NVIDIA para el área de salud, que dependería directamente de Huang, y ambos habrían mantenido una relación , pero ninguno la ha confirmado públicamente. Por ello, la junta directiva debe valorar si los hechos afectan a las normas internas, la supervisión de los directivos o la confianza de los accionistas. En su comunicado del 8 de noviembre, se anunció que un comité de consejeros independientes, asesorado por abogados externos, investigaría el caso. La empresa aseguró que no tenía motivos para creer que sus secretos o la seguridad nacional estuvieran comprometidos y expresó su confianza en Huang, aunque la investigación no equivale a una declaración de culpabilidad, ya que su posible salida también abriría un problema de continuidad. Jensen cofundó NVIDIA en 1993 y ha dirigido su transformación de fabricante de tarjetas gráficas a proveedor clave de los procesadores que impulsan la inteligencia artificial . Su conocimiento y sus relaciones con clientes y socios hacen que sustituirlo no sea una decisión menor, sino más que complicada. Si Elon Musk llegara a contratarlo, xAI sería el encaje más evidente , sobre todo ahora que la empresa necesita una enorme capacidad de cálculo para entrenar modelos como Grok y ofrecer servicios de inteligencia artificial a gran escala. Jensen Huang conoce cómo diseñar y desplegar esa infraestructura, desde las GPU hasta las redes que conectan miles de procesadores para que trabajen coordinados. Su experiencia también abarca los centros de datos y la integración de hardware y software, áreas esenciales para aumentar la potencia de los sistemas y controlar sus costes. La relación tecnológica ya existe, ya que el superordenador Colossus de xAI se construyó con 100.000 GPU Nvidia Hopper y se utiliza para entrenar la familia de modelos Grok. NVIDIA explicó que su plataforma de redes Spectrum-X permitió conectar ese conjunto de procesadores y que xAI planeaba ampliar el sistema hasta 200.000 GPU. Huang podría aportar una visión estratégica para escalar instalaciones de este tipo , mejorar su rendimiento y desarrollar nuevas plataformas. Tesla también podría aprovechar sus conocimientos en chips e inteligencia artificial aplicada a la conducción autónoma y la robótica. Por ahora, la respuesta en X no pasa de ser una muestra pública de interés, ya que la junta de NVIDIA tendrá que decidir qué consecuencias extrae de la investigación y de las informaciones sobre su CEO. Para Musk, incorporar a Huang supondría atraer a un ejecutivo con experiencia directa en la infraestructura que sostiene la carrera por la inteligencia artificial , pero cualquier fichaje depende primero de que se produzca una salida que todavía no se ha confirmado, y de momento son rumores y es poco probable que se haga realidad.

sources.title: ChatGPT is getting verified AI ‘Business Agents’
sources.text: ChatGPT’s new AI agents represent companies and can help with things like comparison shopping. ChatGPT’s new AI agents represent companies and can help with things like comparison shopping. ChatGPT is going to let you chat with verified “Business Agents” that represent a brand to help you with things like comparison shopping. The feature, available first to “eligible” e-commerce and online service businesses in the US, is launching as part of a suite of business-focused features in ChatGPT being announced today in beta . You can start talking with a Business Agent if a business that has created one appears in a response from ChatGPT. While chatting with a custom agent, you can ask about a business’s offerings and ask follow-up questions, like asking about differences between two different products. Businesses can specify a Business Agent’s instructions and provide business context so that the agent knows how to respond. Chats with Business Agents will be clearly labeled and separate from your main ChatGPT conversation, OpenAI says. To help people know that they’re talking with an agent that actually represents the business, companies will be able to claim their organization and get verified through a feature called Business Hub. (OpenAI isn’t sharing specifics about its verification methods because there are different methods for different businesses, VP of monetization Benji Shomair said in a press briefing.) Business Hub will also let companies see insights such as mentions in ChatGPT responses and top “discovery topics” where their business pops up. “Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT,” OpenAI says in a blog post. “We’re starting with the foundations: accurate business information, useful insights and conversations that help people make informed decisions.” As things evolve, “we’ll explore more ways for businesses to connect with customers — directly or through agents and in ChatGPT and beyond. Our goal is to make ChatGPT more useful for people making decisions, and give businesses new ways to participate and grow.”

sources.title: ChatGPT is adding verified 'Business Agents' to help you shop more effectively
sources.text: ChatGPT wants to help businesses better connect to new customers ChatGPT will soon let users talk directly with businesses via new agents that should help you get exactly the information you need. The new "Business Agents" will be verified representatives of the brand you want to contact, with companies able to reserve their own profile using a new Business Hub. OpenAI says the new additions should be useful for comparing different products from the same provider, and discovering new companies and products which otherwise might have been missed. "As people turn to AI to discover products, compare options and make decisions, ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI," the company wrote in a blog post . "Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT. We’re starting with the foundations: accurate business information, useful insights, and conversations that help people make informed decisions." Users will be able to start talking with a Business Agent when one appears in a reply or message from ChatGPT. The reply will include a clickable link which brings up initial information about the company, and a selection of their products or services, as well as contact information. The feature will initially only be available to eligible ecommerce and online service companies in the US, who can register on the new Business Hub, where they can ensure ChatGPT has all the latest information on their products, services and offers. Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed! Companies also be able to get insights into how people interact with their businesses, with the new Hub providing information such as the number of mentions and website clicks a business receives. However user chats with both ChatGPT and Business Agents won't be shared, with a focus on user privacy meaning insights are aggregated, and will only be made available when there are enough conversations or interactions to meet certain thresholds. The company says existing OpenAI Enterprise customers and advertisers can claim their business - and Shopify merchants can connect their store from Business Hub or the Shopify admin to streamline verification. Customers will also be able to sponsor their Business Agent⁠, meaning it will be displayed more prominently in ChatGPT Ads to reach more potential customers - although it notes sponsored placements will be clearly labeled and separate from ChatGPT responses. sources.title: The US is winning the AI race. Jensen Huang could have blown it
sources.text: Nvidia’s chips are powering America’s AI boom. Of course Chinese spies are interested. Nvidia’s chips are powering America’s AI boom. Of course Chinese spies are interested. As espionage targets go, Jensen Huang is perhaps one of the least surprising on Earth. The Nvidia CEO runs one of the world’s most valuable companies, controls the in-demand technology fueling the AI boom, and is cozy with presidents, CEOs, and all manner of important people. He also wears a cool leather jacket. Which makes Huang’s admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy — reportedly while her spying was known to US intelligence and even President Donald Trump — all the more shocking. The fallout goes well beyond his marriage, his reputation, or Nvidia itself. Experts tell The Verge the incident threatens to disrupt the entire US AI industry, potentially jeopardize national security, and could undermine America’s efforts to maintain its fragile technological lead over China in AI. “With those chips, the US lead could vanish in a matter of weeks or months.” Nvidia is the undisputed leader in advanced computer chips, among the AI industry’s scarcest resources. While many ingredients go into building AI models — including talent, energy, capital, and data — top-tier chips are one of the most important, and Nvidia is one of a handful of companies with the expertise to design or manufacture them at the cutting edge. That makes it a gatekeeper to hardware that has become a key bottleneck in global AI development. US companies — including Meta, Anthropic, and OpenAI — are racing to develop chips of their own, in part to reduce their dependence on Nvidia, even as they spend billions securing ever more compute. For China, the US’s main rival at the frontier of AI, that bottleneck is even tighter. To maintain its technological lead, the US has restricted the sale of the most advanced AI chips to the country in the hopes of slowing its progress in the sector, which has been impressive and is thought to trail the US by a matter of months. In response, China has made developing domestic alternatives a strategic national priority, though its leaders still lag Nvidia at the bleeding edge. At the same time, a thriving black market for restricted Nvidia chips has emerged. Experts tell The Verge that China could exploit access to Nvidia to accelerate its own development, or to impede the US development of AI. Getting its hands on more Nvidia chips is the most obvious win for Beijing, says Emily Kilcrease, a senior fellow and director of the energy, economics, and security program at the Center for a New American Security (CNAS) think tank. China has advantages in other parts of the AI race — including abundant energy and a solid ecosystem of open weight models — but without the latest Nvidia chips, it “cannot close the gap with US frontier capabilities,” Kilcrease tells The Verge . “With those chips, the US lead could vanish in a matter of weeks or months.” It is not clear how successful the alleged spying operation has been on that front. There is no public evidence indicating that Huang himself has helped direct restricted Nvidia chips toward China or that sensitive information about them was obtained from him. But companies linked to the alleged spy, Alice Huang — no relation to Jensen — have reportedly enabled at least $7 billion of Nvidia chip sales to China. Brookings fellow Kyle Chan tells The Verge that a concern for US industry could be that companies with alleged ties to China may have had priority access to Nvidia’s latest GPUs. “In a time of chip scarcity,” that would make it much harder for American companies to access them, Chan says. Huang is also a prominent critic of American restrictions on chip sales, and Nvidia spends a formidable amount lobbying in Washington. Last year, he successfully secured White House approval to start exporting Nvidia’s H200 AI GPU chips to “approved customers” in China and other countries. Crucially, Huang also has the ear of President Trump as well as other world leaders, giving him great influence over policy decisions. Hardware is not the only thing of value China could get from close access to Huang, Sunny Cheung, a fellow for China studies at the Jamestown Foundation think tank, tells The Verge . “I actually think too many people are focused on whether somebody managed to steal Nvidia’s trade secrets,” Cheung says, calling it a “very narrow way” of looking at espionage. “I would hope Jensen Huang isn’t foolish enough to hand over the blueprints for Nvidia’s next-generation chips to a suspected Chinese intelligence operative.” The Nvidia CEO’s relationships with other tech executives, senior policymakers, and Trump himself give him an unusually intimate view into how some of the most powerful people in the US are thinking and planning. Beijing could use information on how American companies are planning major infrastructure expansions, their compute requirements, or broad industry trends to inform its own investments and industrial strategy, Cheung says. Huang’s intelligence value could extend well beyond AI, too. “That information alone could be extremely valuable,” says Cheung, pointing to insights Beijing could glean into White House thinking about export controls or the private views of Silicon Valley executives on China and Taiwan. “When so much of America’s AI infrastructure depends on one company, any significant security or governance problem at Nvidia can create uncertainty across the industry.” But helping China advance is only one side of this equation. Disrupting Nvidia — as this scandal clearly has — could destabilize America’s entire AI industry. More than most companies, Nvidia is remarkably closely tied to the identity and reputation of its rockstar CEO. sources.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang? A highly unscientific list of possible successors
sources.text: It’s almost inconceivable that Nvidia would fire its rock star CEO. Yet here we are, on the precipice of this happening. Over at Kalshi, Jensen Huang’s odds of surviving the week are sitting at a lowly 30% . Even though he built one of the world’s most valuable — and, many would argue, dangerously powerful — companies, the tides have completely turned against him. He has confessed to an extramarital affair, but as of Wednesday afternoon it isn’t even clear whom he meant: Alice Huang, the Chinese executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for her country, or Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia executive who reports to him and who, five sources told The New York Times in an explosive new report, was also a paramour. Even if Huang is pushed out as CEO, the board members he has made very rich are unlikely to cut him loose entirely. Barring another shoe dropping, they could keep him on as chairman, a role Nvidia doesn’t currently have. But someone still has to run the company, and there’s no apparent succession plan, which leaves us, like everyone else, to speculate while we wait to see what happens next. While Huang’s 60 direct reports undoubtedly get a closer look, consider this our own parlor game, featuring some obvious and less obvious candidates: Lisa Su . The AMD CEO runs Nvidia’s most credible rival, as well as a distant cousin of Huang. The Information floated her name this week, but why would she leave her job for his? Her company stands to benefit from every day that Nvidia spends distracted by an investigation, congressional briefings, and all the mini dramas that are sure to follow. Her best move might be to send a nice note and keep her current corner office. Eric Schmidt. He was the pick of Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at the Yale School of Management, who we talked with earlier this week. Schmidt could “parachute in tomorrow and do a very good job,” Sonnenfeld said, and perhaps he could. He ran Google from 2001 to 2011, chaired the National Security Commission on AI from 2018 to 2021, and now runs the rocket company Relativity Space. Chips, software, government, rockets — it’s an impressive range. Then again, Schmidt would bring a lot of baggage when it comes to his own extramarital dalliances . It’s hard to see him clearing the board for that reason. Lip-Bu Tan . Intel’s CEO knows chips, and right now he might welcome a very soft landing. Last month, Intel reported third-quarter revenue up 21% to $16.5 billion, then warned its fourth-quarter results would fall short of Wall Street’s forecasts. The AI boom has caused a memory-chip shortage, pushing up PC prices and cutting PC sales. That’s hurt Intel (PC chips are a big part of its business), and its stock plunged 20% in after-hours trading on the warning, having already slid more than 30% since September. A move to a company that’s eating everyone’s lunch would be a pretty amazing escape hatch. Bret Taylor. The former Salesforce co-CEO and OpenAI board chair now runs the AI startup Sierra, and his resume includes a lot of the biggest brands in Silicon Valley. He co-created Google Maps, served as Facebook’s CTO, and chaired Twitter’s board through its sale to Elon Musk. He then took over as OpenAI’s board chair after the “Blip,” Sam Altman’s firing and fast return. When companies need an unflappable, likable adult in the room, they call Taylor. He probably knows nearly every customer Nvidia has, too. Ian Buck. If the board feels strongly about having a “builder” at the helm, they could do worse than the Nvidia VP who helped develop CUDA, the chip software that has become central to Nvidia’s dominance in AI. Analysts and former employees have floated him as a possible successor, and Kalshi traders give him a middling shot . He’s no household name, but the Stanford PhD seems more viable if Huang can can keep that chairman title and push for a successor he can work with. Someone else down the hall. Andrew Bell, Nvidia’s senior vice president of hardware engineering, arrived 25 years ago as a fresh Cornell grad and has been on an upward trajectory at the company ever since. Like Buck and dozens of other executives who are presumably being scrutinized, he reports directly to Huang. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is the insider most often named, but analysts say she isn’t necessarily a natural successor as an innovator and visionary, and Bell has the chip pedigree. The wild card? Lori Huang . Nobody has floated her, but hear us out: Jensen met his wife as lab partners at Oregon State, so she has been working with him since before Nvidia existed. After graduating, she worked at Silicon Graphics as a micro chip engineer (making more money than her husband, he has said), then scaled back to raise the couple’s family, and she now co-leads the family trusts. If the board wants continuity, they could do worse than a humbler Huang who is also a brainiac. There’s a reason they say that behind every great man is a great woman (and vice versa). sources.title: Motorola Signature 27 terá novas funções do Gemini Intelligence; confira
sources.text: O que o novo Motorola Signature 27 entrega na prática? Conversamos com uma executiva da marca sobre inteligência artificial, a nova geração do Snapdragon e como. O Google confirmou na terça-feira (10) a chegada de novos recursos desenvolvidos para Gemini Intelligence a mais dispositivos Android de última geração, entre os quais o Motorola Signature 27. Além do top de linha lançado na semana passada , os celulares da série Pixel 10 também terão acesso às ferramentas de IA avançadas . Apresentada durante o The Android 2026, a plataforma concorrente da Apple Intelligence reúne recursos baseados no Gemini que fazem o smartphone “trabalhar mais para o usuário” , de acordo com a companhia de Mountain View. Ela já estava disponível em modelos da nova geração da linha Galaxy Z, na série Galaxy S26 e no Pixel 11. No novo smartphone premium da Motorola, será possível obter assistência avançada do Gemini para diversas atividades. O recurso Rambler “transforma pensamentos falados em texto limpo e organizado em tempo real” , como explicou o Google, em comunicado. Já com a Assistência do Dispositivo, o Gemini Intelligence atua como um suporte técnico personalizado . A IA pode liberar espaço no armazenamento externo, verificar quais apps têm acesso às informações de localização e desativar distrações, garantindo que as chamadas importantes sejam atendidas. “O Gemini entende profundamente o seu dispositivo para que possa agir como seu especialista pessoal”, afirmou a gigante das buscas. Neste último recurso, basta descrever que tipo de assistência você precisa. Para quem tem um smartphone Pixel com Gemini Intelligence , as novidades incluem sugestões proativas no Android Auto . Se o usuário receber uma mensagem perguntando sobre o local de um evento, por exemplo, a IA pode pesquisar a informação no email de confirmação e sugerir o envio do endereço. No Pixel Watch, a estreia será o criador de widgets detalhado acima. A atualização estará disponível nas próximas semanas, ajudando a manter informações de maior utilidade sempre à vista . A plataforma de IA avançada também está integrada aos Googlebooks. Siga no TecMundo e conheça os novos notebooks com o software do Google . sources.title: Recursos do Gemini Intelligence chegam a celulares Motorola com novidades
sources.text: O Google anunciou a expansão do Gemini Intelligence para mais dispositivos Android . A novidade marca a estreia da tecnologia no Motorola Signature 27, que teve a pré-venda iniciada nos Estados Unidos em 19 de novembro. A atualização também chega ao Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL e Pixel 10 Pro Fold por meio do Pixel Drop mais recente. O anúncio foi feito por Karthik Thirumalai, diretor de produtos de IA para Android. Antes da expansão, o Gemini Intelligence já estava disponível no Pixel 11 e nos modelos Samsung Galaxy S26, S26+, S26 Ultra, Z Fold8, Z Fold8 Ultra e Z Flip8. A atualização traz novos recursos , como a criação de widgets personalizados e o controle de configurações do celular por comandos de voz, além de ampliar funções existentes , como a organização de textos falados. A automação de tarefas também chega a novos países, incluindo Reino Unido, Índia e Japão. Nesses locais, usuários maiores de 18 anos podem pedir ao Gemini que faça reservas em restaurantes, solicite comida e chame serviços de transporte. O Google também ampliou os recursos de assistência técnica e integração entre dispositivos . O Device Assistance ajuda a localizar e alterar configurações do sistema por voz. Já o Create My Widget gera painéis personalizados a partir de descrições em texto. A empresa ainda prepara novidades para o Pixel Watch e o Android Auto, além da integração com o Googlebook, primeiro laptop desenvolvido nativamente para o Gemini Intelligence. Os recursos atendem a diferentes tarefas, desde a organização de mensagens até o gerenciamento de configurações do aparelho. Confira as principais ferramentas: Rambler : transforma pensamentos e anotações faladas em textos organizados em tempo real. Integrado ao teclado Gboard, o recurso corrige e estrutura o conteúdo durante a transcrição. A ferramenta chega ao motorola signature 27 e aos aparelhos da linha Pixel 10; Create My Widget : gera widgets personalizados para a tela inicial a partir de instruções em texto. O usuário pode pedir, por exemplo, um painel para acompanhar gastos mensais, uma contagem regressiva ou um roteiro de viagem. A inteligência artificial consulta informações do Gmail, Google Agenda e Pesquisa Google. O recurso também chegará ao Pixel Watch nas próximas semanas; Device Assistance : funciona como um assistente técnico integrado ao Android. Com comandos de voz, o usuário pode pedir ajuda para liberar espaço no armazenamento, verificar quais aplicativos têm acesso à localização ou configurar modos de foco para reduzir distrações. A ferramenta requer Android 17 ou posterior em dispositivos compatíveis; Integração entre telas e Android Auto : conecta informações de diferentes aplicativos para apresentar sugestões contextuais. No Android Auto, por exemplo, o sistema pode identificar uma mensagem sobre um compromisso, localizar o e-mail de confirmação correspondente e sugerir o endereço do evento na tela do veículo. O recurso requer o aplicativo Gemini configurado em celulares Pixel compatíveis. Automação de tarefas : o aplicativo Gemini ganhou suporte ampliado para executar tarefas cotidianas, como solicitar refeições, chamar transporte e fazer reservas em restaurantes. A funcionalidade chegou a usuários do Reino Unido, Índia e Japão. Se você gostou do conteúdo, talvez também se interesse por conferir “ Como o Gemini pode deixar seu celular Galaxy ainda mais inteligente ”.

stories.title: Universidade chinesa compra chips H200 da Nvidia apesar de restrição
stories.summary: Registros de compras mostram como instituições da China usam revendedores locais para alugar e obter chips de IA restritos O post Universidade chinesa compra chips H200 da Nvidia apesar de restrição apareceu primeiro em Olhar Digital .

sources.name: Olhar Digital IA
sources.title: Universidade chinesa compra chips H200 da Nvidia apesar de restrição
sources.text: Uma universidade chinesa com fortes vínculos com o Exército de Libertação Popular comprou dois chips H200 da Nvidia, apesar de integrar a lista americana de instituições sujeitas a restrições comerciais. A aquisição, realizada em outubro, expõe as dificuldades de Washington para limitar o acesso da China a semicondutores avançados. A Northwestern Polytechnical University pagou 874,7 mil yuans (cerca de R$ 731,6 mil) pelos processadores , segundo registros públicos de compras. A operação foi registrada em 21 de outubro e intermediada pela empresa chinesa Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology. O H200 está entre os chips mais avançados da Nvidia para treinar e executar sistemas de inteligência artificial (IA). A universidade integra o grupo Seven Sons of National Defense, formado por instituições chinesas com histórico de pesquisas militares, incluindo estudos sobre aeronaves, mísseis e satélites. Além da compra, a Northwestern obteve acesso a processadores da Nvidia por meio de contratos de aluguel de capacidade computacional com empresas chinesas. Em janeiro, sua escola de cibersegurança firmou dois acordos de sete meses para utilizar servidores equipados com oito H200 cada. Os contratos foram avaliados em 441,7 mil yuans (cerca de R$ 369,4 mil) e 441 mil yuans (cerca de R$ 368,9 mil) e previam o ajuste fino de modelos de IA e treinamento por aprendizado por reforço. A instituição também alugou servidores com oito chips A100 e oito A800. Em abril, outro instituto da universidade contratou serviços computacionais que exigiam pelo menos 24 A100, por 375 mil yuans (cerca de R$ 313,7 mil). O serviço seria usado em simulações de estruturas e dinâmica de fluidos. Os registros identificaram empresas chinesas como fornecedoras, mas não informaram a origem dos processadores nem a localização dos servidores. Uma análise da Reuters de 26 registros de compras e documentos corporativos identificou outras instituições chinesas que adquiriram chips sujeitos a restrições americanas ou contrataram serviços computacionais equipados com esses componentes. O Departamento de Comércio dos Estados Unidos incluiu a Northwestern na lista de restrições comerciais conhecida como Entity List em 2001, por seu suposto envolvimento em atividades de proliferação de mísseis e pesquisas militares. Em 2019, Washington endureceu as regras, tornando improvável a aprovação de licenças para exportar tecnologias controladas à universidade. Em janeiro de 2026, o governo de Donald Trump começou a permitir algumas exportações de H200 para a China mediante análise individual. A flexibilização, porém, não suspendeu as restrições às instituições da Entity List. As regras também exigem medidas para impedir o acesso remoto de organizações proibidas e usuários militares aos chips exportados. Parlamentares americanos temem que esses processadores acelerem o desenvolvimento de tecnologias militares chinesas, como sistemas para projeto de armas e análise de inteligência. O CEO da Nvidia, Jensen Huang , defende regras mais flexíveis para as vendas ao país. Segundo ele, manter as exportações ajuda a preservar a liderança tecnológica dos Estados Unidos e a dependência dos clientes chineses em relação à tecnologia americana. Democratas e republicanos defendem controles mais rigorosos, incluindo rastreamento dos chips e maior supervisão do Congresso. Três presidentes republicanos de comissões parlamentares solicitaram um briefing com Huang em 18 de novembro para discutir seus supostos contatos com uma pessoa apontada como agente de inteligência chinesa. Na semana anterior, a Reuters havia informado que pequenas quantidades de H200 chegaram à China por rotas indiretas, enquanto Pequim ainda não havia autorizado importações em grande escala. Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

sources.title: Investigação revela que universidade chinesa driblou restrições e comprou chips de IA da Nvidia
sources.text: Polêmica com CEO da Nvidia envolve suspeita de espionagem e balança o mercado de IA Uma universidade chinesa que possui ligações com o Exército de Libertação Popular comprou chips de IA da Nvidia mesmo fazendo parte de uma lista de instituições com restrições comerciais de exportação do governo dos Estados Unidos , revelou a Reuters nesta quarta-feira (11). As aquisições aconteceram em outubro. A investigação do veículo avaliou registros de compras que mostram que a Northwestern Polytechnical University gastou 874.700 yuans, o equivalente a pouco mais de R$ 683 mil pela cotação do dia, para comprar dois chips H200 fabricados pela gigante americana , um dos componentes mais poderosos da marca. A operação foi intermediada pela fornecedora Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology. Questionadas pela agência de notícias, a instituição de ensino, a Nvidia e o órgão americano de controle das exportações não se pronunciaram. Já a fornecedora não foi localizada. Localizada na cidade de Xian, a universidade pública tem pesquisas nas áreas de aeronaves militares, satélites e mísseis. Por causa dessas atividades e do histórico de trabalhos relacionados à defesa de Pequim, a Northwestern Polytechnical foi adicionada à lista de proibições em 2001 . A reportagem afirma ter encontrado 26 registros corporativos e de compras feitas por universidades e entidades de pesquisa chinesas somente este ano , utilizando tecnologia da Nvidia sujeita a restrições por meio de fornecedores nacionais. Muitos dos clientes tinham relações com a indústria de defesa ou pesquisa militar. A divulgação ocorre em meio à suposta operação de espionagem chinesa que teria como alvo Jensen Huang, CEO da gigante dos semicondutores. Ele defendeu a redução de restrições à venda de chips de IA alegando que a liderança tecnológica americana não seria afetada. Em uma investigação separada, o The New York Times levanta a possibilidade da existência de falhas no controle de exportação de chips de IA . Conforme o jornal, duas empresas chinesas autorizadas a comprar os componentes possuem escritórios vazios e ligações com fornecedores militares sancionados. Além delas, outras companhias, incluindo marcas conhecidas, teriam sido autorizadas a realizar a aquisição dos chips H200. Com isso, o relatório questiona se o Departamento de Comércio americano estaria aprovando os pedidos de compra automaticamente , sem investigar as ligações com Pequim. “Tenho muitas preocupações de que nem o Departamento de Comércio nem a Nvidia estejam fazendo a devida diligência necessária para garantir que os termos da licença estejam sendo cumpridos”, afirmou Liza Tobin, ex-diretora para a China do Conselho de Segurança Nacional da Casa Branca, ao jornal. Siga no TecMundo e confira mais desdobramentos do caso extraconjugal do CEO da Nvidia . Com informações de Reuters e The New York Times .
